implementerProof.how: Every one of the five entries of implement.json's proof array was driven again from scratch, never by re-running the implementer's own scaffolding. (1) The loader proof: I built the binary myself (go -C packages/daemon build -o $TMPDIR/t934/legion ./cmd/legion) and built four legion.yaml fixtures of my own from deploy/kubernetes/daemon/legion.yaml.example with deploy/kubernetes/operator-route/pod.yml indented under runtime.kubernetes.pod, the way scripts/e2e/stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:1404 does it — account unfilled, audience unfilled, both unfilled, both filled — and ran legion start --check-config on each. The account-unfilled fixture printed the message implement.json quotes, byte for byte, and exited 1; the both-filled one printed 'Config OK: project=WIDGETS' and exited 0. (2) The live-proof gate: I ran all three scripts myself with the variable unset, under a PATH whose first kubectl appends its argv to a file and echoes the same line to stdout, so the ordering is visible in the run's own output rather than inferred. All three refused with 'pod-service-account: LEGION_E2E_POD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT is unset: …' and exited 1; stage4b and claude-backend-sandbox.sh made no kubectl call at all (the recorder file was never created), and stage4a's six calls all appear after the refusal line, under '== teardown', against its own run label. (3) and (4) The replacement decision and the cache sweep: I re-ran go test ./internal/runtime/sandbox/... ./internal/config/... (ok, 223s and cached) and then mutation-tested the five claims on a copy of packages/daemon under $TMPDIR — dropping the accountDrifted term from relaunch, moving it inside the !installing guard, comparing the two accounts raw instead of through serviceAccountOr, dropping the warning from warnPodDrift, and dropping the term from reconcileCachePod. Each mutation was caught by the named test, so the regression locks are real and not tautologies. (5) The e2e library and the grep: bun test scripts/e2e/lib gave 737 pass / 2 fail, both the docker-dependent cases in scripts/e2e/lib/nats-stream.test.ts ('error: Executable not found in $PATH: "docker"'), which is this pod and not the change; the acceptance grep printed nothing (exit 1), and a plain grep for legion-worker over the same two paths leaves only the image repository ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion-worker, two ConfigMap names in namespace-rig.test.ts and a skill path, none of them a ServiceAccount.

failures.criterion: R5 / A2, the LEGION_E2E_POD_FILE lane: the account a deployment's pod block names is read by one rule, the rule this change wrote into scripts/e2e/lib/deployment-pod-block-verdict.jq — an absent service_account and an empty one both mean the namespace's `default`.
failures.evidence: scripts/e2e/stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:3143, which this change adds, computes `pod_account=$(jq -r '.service_account // "default"' "$pod_block")`. jq's `//` is false only for null and false, so an empty service_account survives it: measured, `echo '{"service_account":""}' | jq -r '.service_account // "default"'` prints the empty string, where the `def account` this same change added to scripts/e2e/lib/deployment-pod-block-verdict.jq:53-56 prints `default` for the same input, and so does the daemon (serviceAccountOr, packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/sandbox.go:678-680). Both consumers of pod_account are then wrong for such a block, and both reject a pod that is right: shape_problems (stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:2016, --arg account) and the deployment-pod-block checkpoint's identity (stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:3540, want="system:serviceaccount:$namespace:$pod_account"). Driven, not read: I extracted shape_problems with scripts/e2e/lib/script-functions.ts and ran it on the runtime's own golden operator-route pod with spec.serviceAccountName set to `default`, which is what such a block's pods really run as. With pod_account as the script computes it (empty) it printed `serviceAccountName default`, failing the pod-shape checkpoint on a correct pod; with pod_account=default, what the verdict jq says the same block means, it printed no serviceAccountName line. The note at stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:3120 spells the same field a third way (`// "the namespace default"`), which prints nothing at all for an empty one. The red test is scripts/e2e/lib/stage4b-pods.test.ts's `the account a deployment's pod block names`, three cases driving `block_account()` out of the script with the file's own scriptFunctions harness, as its shape_problems, record_stream and pod_shape_verdict tests are driven: `bun test scripts/e2e/lib/stage4b-pods.test.ts` is 56 pass / 3 fail at commit 7ca6678fcf18, each failure `stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh defines no block_account()`. The test discriminates rather than only demanding the name: wrapping today's expression in `block_account() { jq -r '.service_account // "default"' "$pod_block"; }` and running it on the three blocks prints `legion-infra-worker`, `default` and `''`, so the first two cases pass and the empty-account case still fails on `''` against `default`. The fix is the one rule in the three places, plus that function for the test to reach.

proof.criterion: A1 (loader): `legion start --check-config` refuses runtime.kubernetes.pod.service_account still holding ${POD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT}, and loads the operator route once it is filled.
proof.surface: The operator's own command, the real built binary on a legion.yaml carrying deploy/kubernetes/operator-route/pod.yml under runtime.kubernetes.pod — the shape scripts/e2e/stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:1404 writes for a live run.
proof.command: go -C packages/daemon build -o $TMPDIR/t934/legion ./cmd/legion; then, on four fixtures built from deploy/kubernetes/daemon/legion.yaml.example with pod.yml indented six spaces under `pod:` (account unfilled, audience unfilled, both unfilled, both filled): $TMPDIR/t934/legion start --check-config --config ./legion.yaml
proof.observed: Account unfilled: exit 1, `legion start: runtime.kubernetes.pod.service_account "${POD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT}" is an unfilled placeholder: put the ServiceAccount the pods run as in its place`. Both filled: exit 0, `Config OK: project=WIDGETS`. The whole chain holds too: I extracted render_operator_pod from scripts/e2e/stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh with scripts/e2e/lib/script-functions.ts, ran it with pod_service_account=legion-infra-worker and gateway_audience=gw-aud, and fed its $work/pod.yml into a legion.yaml the same way — `Config OK: project=WIDGETS`, exit 0, so what a live proof renders is what the daemon's own loader accepts.
proof.negativeControl: The same fixture with the audience placeholder left unfilled instead refuses with its own message, `runtime.kubernetes.pod.volumes[1].projected.sources[0].service_account_token.audience "${MODEL_TOKEN_AUDIENCE}" is an unfilled placeholder`, exit 1, so the new refusal is the account's own and not a blanket one; and render_operator_pod run against a copy of pod.yml whose placeholder was already replaced refuses with `the operator route's pod.yml has no ServiceAccount ${POD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT} to fill with the run's`, exit 1.

proof.criterion: A2 (R5): each of stage4a-sandbox-runtime.sh, stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh and claude-backend-sandbox.sh exits non-zero naming LEGION_E2E_POD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT, before any kubectl call.
proof.surface: Each live proof's own CLI, with every other required input set, under a PATH whose first kubectl appends its argv to a recorder file and echoes the same line to stdout, so the refusal's place in the run's output is read rather than inferred.
proof.command: env -u LEGION_E2E_POD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT PATH=$TMPDIR/t934/bin:$PATH <the other required inputs> bash scripts/e2e/<script>.sh, for each of the three
proof.observed: All three exited 1 with `pod-service-account: LEGION_E2E_POD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT is unset: set it to the ServiceAccount the deployment's pods run as` and each script's own FAIL line naming the variable. stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh and claude-backend-sandbox.sh made no kubectl call at all — the recorder file was never created. stage4a-sandbox-runtime.sh's recorder held six calls, every one of them printed after the refusal line and under its `== teardown` heading, each against its own run label legion.dev/project=s4a-<run>. The helper itself refuses an upper-case name, a name with a space, a leading `-`, a trailing `.`, `_`, `/` and a 254-character name, and prints a 253-character one and `a.b-c9` unchanged; a refusal names the variable and never its value.
proof.negativeControl: The same stage4a run with LEGION_E2E_POD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT=legion-infra-worker passes that gate and refuses further down, on an input this pod cannot supply (`reading LEGION_E2E_PREVIOUS_IMAGE …'s labels failed`, the stub docker), so the gate is the account's and not an unconditional stop.

proof.criterion: A1 (R1, R2, R3): a launch into a live issue or controller pod on another ServiceAccount replaces the pod on the same Sandbox, a plugin install included; the cache sweep makes a cache pod again for the same reason, keeping its Sandbox and volume; a matching pod, and `default` against an unset configuration, are kept.
proof.surface: The daemon's Kubernetes runtime through its own rig against a fake API server — the only surface a worker pod reaches, and the surface this issue's acceptance names (the live cluster proof is INFRA-321's migrate children).
proof.command: cd packages/daemon && go test ./internal/runtime/sandbox/... ./internal/config/... ; then five mutations on a copy of packages/daemon under $TMPDIR, each run against the test that claims it
proof.observed: ok github.com/sjawhar/legion/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox 223.396s, ok …/internal/config (cached). The mutations show the locks are real, not tautologies: dropping `accountDrifted` from relaunch's replace expression fails four subtests of TestARelaunchReplacesAPodRunningAnotherServiceAccount; putting it inside the `!installing` guard fails `an installing Resume replaces a pod on another ServiceAccount` alone; comparing the two accounts raw instead of through serviceAccountOr fails `no configured ServiceAccount and a pod on default` and the boot-warning test; deleting the account warning from warnPodDrift fails TestTheBootReconciliationWarnsOfEachPodRunningAnotherServiceAccount; dropping the term from reconcileCachePod fails both `a cache pod on another ServiceAccount is made again` (the Sandbox is neither suspended nor set Running again, and the written template's account is "") and `a cache pod on another ServiceAccount serving a stream waits`.
proof.negativeControl: The kept cases are in the same table and assert the pod UID is unchanged: `an issue pod already on the configured ServiceAccount`, `no configured ServiceAccount and a pod on default`, and the cache's `a cache pod on the configured ServiceAccount is left alone`, which asserts no Sandbox or pod is written at all — so the term does not replace every pod.

proof.criterion: A2 (R5): bun test scripts/e2e/lib passes, the acceptance grep finds no ServiceAccount named legion-worker under scripts/e2e or deploy/kubernetes/operator-route, and scripts/e2e/README.md names the variable.
proof.surface: The repository's own bun test runner and the greps the acceptance names, run in the issue workspace.
proof.command: bun test scripts/e2e/lib; git grep -nE '(service_account|serviceAccountName|serviceAccount)[":= ]+legion-worker|"legion-worker"|`legion-worker`' -- scripts/e2e deploy/kubernetes/operator-route; grep -c LEGION_E2E_POD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT scripts/e2e/README.md; grep -rn legion-worker scripts/e2e deploy/kubernetes/operator-route
proof.observed: 737 pass, 2 fail across 61 files, both of them scripts/e2e/lib/nats-stream.test.ts's docker cases, failing with `error: Executable not found in $PATH: "docker"` — this pod carries no docker. The acceptance grep printed nothing and exited 1. The README names the variable 12 times. The unrestricted grep for legion-worker over the same two paths returns only the image repository `ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion-worker`, the two ConfigMap names in scripts/e2e/lib/namespace-rig.test.ts and one skill path, so the acceptance grep's silence is not hiding a spelling it cannot see.
proof.negativeControl: scripts/e2e/lib/stage4b-pods.test.ts's `a pod on another ServiceAccount departs` is the control for the rule that replaced the literal: it sets the golden operator-route pod's serviceAccountName to another-account and the run's pod-shape rule names it, so the comparison still has teeth after the literal went.

proof.criterion: A3 (R6): docs/kubernetes.md names account drift where it lists what replaces a pod, and a unit test asserts the account warning's line.
proof.surface: The documentation as a reader opens it, and the runtime's own log through the rig.
proof.command: grep -n ServiceAccount docs/kubernetes.md, read at :1605-1632, :2883, :3769 and :4286; cd packages/daemon && go test ./internal/runtime/sandbox/ -run ServiceAccount -v
proof.observed: The pinning section carries the warning verbatim at :1616-1618, says the replacement is outside image drift's install exemption (:1621), names the controller's pod (:1622) and states the unset-is-default rule (:1623); the launch-replacement list at :1627 names another ServiceAccount; the repository-cache paragraph at :2883 names a new account beside a new image; `What ends an issue pod's disk` at :3769 names another ServiceAccount; the runtime.kubernetes.pod reference at :4286 says service_account may not hold a ${…} placeholder. The logged line the docs quote and the fmt.Sprintf in warnPodDrift are the same string, and TestTheBootReconciliationWarnsOfEachPodRunningAnotherServiceAccount asserts it character for character.
proof.negativeControl: The same test asserts the Sandbox whose pod already runs as the configured account is warned of zero times, and the cache Sandbox zero times, so the warning is drift's and not a line printed for every Sandbox; and deleting it from warnPodDrift turns that test red, while the image warning's own prefix count in watch_test.go stays green, which is what keeps the image line byte-identical.
